question: Does the `tag` console command (CSetCountryControllerCommand) give the top bar and the country views the new country's pictures? And where does an edit box whose font is a `font = { }` entry - the console's console_edit, in FPS_Font - put its line?

addresses.name: CSetCountryControllerCommand::Execute
addresses.comment: CCommand slot 6. The human (FindHumanById, +0x4C) loses its 'primary local' byte (+0x28, `Human X unset as primary local`). **The country it had** (+0x44/+0x48), where no other human holds it: played_countries[it] = 0, its CEU3AI's +0x2C = 1 (the AI takes it), `AI will control <name>`. An intelligence refresh requested. Where the human is unknown or the new id (+0x40) is 0, `Attempted to assign ... to nonextistant human` and stop; otherwise the human is made primary local where no other human of that country is (`Human X set as primary local`), **its country = +0x3C/+0x40**, and **where it is this machine's human** (the session's +0x6C, the in-game screen's slot 18): played_countries[new] = 1, **state->player and the map's player = the country**, its AI's +0x2C = 0, `Local player will control <name>`; another machine's: played_countries[new] = 2, its AI's +0x2C = 0, `Remote player will control <name>`. Every arm that changes a controller sets the state's controllers_changed (+0xC0), which is what refreshes the lobby's panel. **The tail, read 2026-11-15** (0x6D3F82..the bare ret at 0x6D42E5): (1) where the session's lobby_reopened (+0x236) is set, CGameState::TurnOffCountryAi(state, local = the session's +0x6C equals the human, the new country's tag and id) (0x6D4048); (2) the persistent whose id is at 0x171042C/0x1710430 - the lobby's CLobbyInterface, given that id by CGameSetup's constructor - looked up in the id table its type selects (0x1268 or below the low one, above it the high) and, where it exists, its slot 11 (CGameSetup's CLobbyInterface table slot 11, VA 0x714100, the multiplayer list's row for that country: player_shield and `name (tag)`, read only in outline) called with the new country; (3) the in-game screen's slot 65, the top bar, and where there is one its outliner's force_rebuild (CTopBar +0x378, COutLiner +0x7C) set to 1. **That is all**: every direct call in the body (listing 0x6D3390..0x6D42E5) is FindHumanById, the logging, the game state's lazy constructor, CountryNameOfTag, FindPersistentById and 0x683830, and every indirect one is a stream, the game state's deleting destructor, GetSession, the lobby's slot 11 or the top bar's getter - **nothing gives the top bar or the country views a picture**: CInGameIdler::ApplyCountrySkins is not reached and no country view's slot 9 is called. So a `tag` keeps the pictures of the country the session was entered with (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topbar.md, *The skin*). Bare ret.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole (headless DecompileAt on a private copy) and the call list taken off the listing 0x6D3390..0x6D42E5 (scripts/disasm.py). The three tail steps read on the listing: 0x6D3F8D GetSession, cmp byte [eax+0x236]; push id,tag,(id==session+0x6C); call 0x683830 at 0x6D4048; 0x6D404D..0x6D4106 the 0x171042C id looked up (FindPersistentById 0xA9DA00) and [vtable+0x2C] called; 0x6D42B3 mov ecx,[state+0xBE8]; call [edx+0x104]; mov ecx,[eax+0x378]; mov byte [ecx+0x7C],1. Shown wrong by any call in the body this list misses - a jump table or a call through a pointer the decompile hides would do it; scripts/findRefs.py --callers 0x662430 gives the one call from CInGameIdler::Enter.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ApplyCountrySkins
addresses.comment: **The played country's own pictures on the country views and on the top bar, once, as a session comes up.** First each of the six country views (+0xD00, the loop ends at 0x18 bytes) is asked its slot 9 - CCountryView::UpdateCountrySkin, country_bg_<TAG>.dds behind it (CProductionView's slot 9, VA 0x8053B0, is a bare jmp to that body). Then, for the top bar (+0x1318): 'gfx/interface/skins/topbar_' + the played country's tag as text (the current game state's player, made by the inlined singleton accessor where it does not exist yet) + '.dds', and **only where FileExists (0x66B3A0) finds it** a sprite is made of it - PictureSprite_Construct with the type StringHashFind('GFX_topbar_bg') from the sprite registry (graphics +0xA0) - and set on the icon `topbar_bg` of the bar's window (CTopBar +0x20; CFixedWindow::FindIcon, slot 17) through the icon's slot 56, and shown (slot 13) where the window's shown byte (+0x5B) is set. **The icon is not tested for a miss**: a mod with the file and no `topbar_bg` icon would call slot 56 on null. Where the file is not there the icon keeps what its sprite names - `skins/topbar_generic` in topbar.gfx. **One caller, CInGameIdler::Enter (VA 0x66153B)**, after the top bar exists; nothing else references it and it is in no virtual table. **A change of the played country in play does not reach it** (read 2026-11-15): CSetCountryControllerCommand::Execute, which the `tag` console command posts, was read whole and calls neither this nor any view's slot 9, and **no other caller of the views' slot 9 was found** - of the 1007 slot-9 call sites in the image (scripts/slotcalls.py 9), the only one through the idler's views (+0xD00) is this function's, and the five inside the views' own methods (CEspionageView::BuildTooltip, CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip three times, CProductionView::IsShown) push an argument where UpdateCountrySkin takes none, so are other objects' slot 9. So the bar and the six views keep the pictures of the country the session was entered with. The statistics ledger's own country_bg picture (CStatisticsLedger_ApplyCountrySkin) is made by its constructor, at each opening, and follows the country played. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-topbar.md, *The skin*.
addresses.evidence: findRefs --callers 0x662430: one call, 0x66153B. CSetCountryControllerCommand::Execute read whole (its own entry). slotcalls.py 9 --touches 0xD00: seven functions, of which only this one indexes the idler's views (the others are ApplyCustomGameSettings, GetElementTooltip, SyncOutliner, LedgerPage_Buildings, CSplitTroopsEffect::Execute and 0x41E510, each calling slot 9 on its own list's objects); a scan of every slot-9 site inside the seven country-view classes' table functions found five, each with a push before the call. 0x8053B0 disassembles to `jmp 0x6EB4F0`. Shown wrong by a caller reaching a view through a pointer neither scan sees - a view held elsewhere than +0xD00 and asked its slot 9 by a function outside the views' tables.

addresses.name: CGameState::TurnOffCountryAi
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CGameState::TurnOffCountryAi(CGameState* this, bool local, int countryTag, int countryId)
addresses.comment: **A country handed to a person: marked played and, on a session that posts commands, its AI taken away.** played_countries[countryId] (+0xBCC) = 1 where `local`, otherwise 2. Then, where the in-game screen's session (slot 18) has may_post_commands (+0x34) set: the country's CEU3AI found in ai_agents (+0x114..+0x118, the entry whose +0x24 is the id) and erased from it (0x68D990), the country's `ai` pointer in the country database set to null, and `AI has been turned off for <name>` logged (gamestate.cpp). One caller, CSetCountryControllerCommand::Execute (0x6D4048), only where the session's lobby_reopened (+0x236) is set. ret 0xC. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Likely: decompiled whole; `ret 0xc` at 0x683A49, the three arguments read at [ebp+8], [ebp+0xC], [ebp+0x10] (0x683856..0x683867: sete on the bool, inc, store into [state+0xBCC][id*4]); findRefs --callers 0x683830 gives 0x6D4048 alone; in no virtual table (vtable.py --holding). What `played = 2` means (a remote player) is inferred from Execute's own arms, which write 1 for the local human and 2 for another machine's. Shown wrong if 0x68D990 is not the vector's erase, which was not read.

addresses.name: TrueTypeFont_DrawTextToTexture
addresses.signature: void* __fastcall TrueTypeFont_DrawTextToTexture(void* font@ECX, void* texture@stack:4, int* textureSize@stack:8, int* shownSize@stack:0xC, Hoi3CString* text@stack:0x10, void* background@stack:0x14, int maxWidth@stack:0x18, int maxHeight@stack:0x1C, int* border@stack:0x20, int format@stack:0x24, bool fit@stack:0x28, int passes@stack:0x2C, bool notFixedSize@stack:0x30) @EAX
addresses.comment: **Slot 6 of the font a `font = { }` block makes** (table VA 0x1606118, no RTTI) - the TrueType counterpart of CEU3BitmapFont::DrawTextToTexture, with the same twelve arguments, which CTextSprite::RenderText pushes (VA 0xAB58BB..0xAB58FF: !fixedsize, 1, fixedsize, format, &border, height, width, background, ...). So **a textBoxType or an editBoxType whose font is a `font = { }` entry is drawn by this, not by the bitmap font's routine** - the console's `console_edit` in FPS_Font among them. The DrawText flags start at 0. maxWidth and maxHeight both given: flags DT_WORDBREAK|DT_NOCLIP (0x110) and `fit` forced on; a maxWidth of nought becomes border.x + 1, a maxHeight of nought border.y + 1 (flags 0x110). `fit`: flags 0x110. **notFixedSize false (a fixedsize box): flags 0x115**, adding DT_CENTER and DT_VCENTER. Then the format: 0 clears DT_CENTER and DT_RIGHT (left), 1 DT_RIGHT, 2 DT_CENTER. Where the flags have DT_WORDBREAK and a byte at [esp+0x1F] (cleared only when maxWidth was nought) is set, the text is first laid out by CTextLayout at maxWidth - 3 * border.x. **The rectangle**: left border.x, top border.y, right maxWidth - border.x, bottom maxHeight - border.y; with text, a DT_CALCRECT pass (flags | 0x400) on a copy. Not `fit`: the shown size (third argument) = the measured right + 2 * border.x by the measured bottom + 2 * border.y, the rectangle the measured one widened to it. `fit`: the shown size = maxWidth - border.x by maxHeight - border.y (or border.y + the measured bottom where that is more; and a measured top above border.y moves it), the rectangle's right and bottom that less the border again. The texture is the shown size rounded up to powers of two (the width times `passes` where notFixedSize is set). With a background, it is drawn first (0xB1D5C0 with the shown size and the border where notFixedSize is set, otherwise 0xB1CA50), then **ID3DXFont::DrawTextA (the font's +0x30, slot 14) with no sprite, the text, the rectangle, the flags and the font's colour (+0x70)**, `passes` times, the rectangle moved maxWidth right each time. **So the line's cell stands at the rectangle's top, border.y down, set left, and is never centred up and down unless the box is fixedsize** - an edit box passes fixedsize 0. With the display object put the border in from the box's corner, an edit box's line in such a font has its cell top-left the border twice in each way. Returns the texture. A global byte (0x1BEA534), where set, saves the texture as text.tga once and clears itself.
addresses.evidence: Likely: the flag arithmetic and the rectangle read on the listing (0xB1B9E2..0xB1BA6B, 0xB1BBC0..0xB1BCEF), the DrawText calls at 0xB1BEDF and 0xB1C39F (push colour [edi+0x70], flags [esp+0x18 after pushes], &rect, length, text, 0, font [edi+0x30]; call [vtable+0x38]); `ret 0x30` at 0xB1BF6C and 0xB1C4E4; slot 6 of VA 0x1606118 read off the table; the caller's pushes read at 0xAB58BB..0xAB58FF. The rest from the decompile, whose stack is confused around the two drawing arms - the background routines 0xB1D5C0 and 0xB1CA50 were not read, and whether ID3DXFont honours DT_VCENTER without DT_SINGLELINE is Direct3D's and not this executable's. Shown wrong by an edit box passing fixedsize 1 to RenderText (EditBox_RefreshText 0xA90140 was read by the textrest agent to pass 0), or by a screenshot of the original's console putting its line elsewhere than 20 below and 20 right of console_edit's corner.

slots_noted: TrueTypeFont_DrawTextToTexture is slot 6 of the TrueType font's table (VA 0x1606118), which has no RTTI class, as TrueTypeFont_DrawText (slot 8) and TrueTypeFont_CreateDeviceFont (slot 5) already are recorded.
